name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: selection and input

Identify the data first: free text, ordered choice, bounded quantity, binary state, color, or editable image. Match precision and range to the control, then check keyboard, focus, validation, locale, and accessibility behavior. Platform-specific styles are consequential: a macOS combo box, a tvOS PIN screen, and a watchOS crown picker solve different tasks.

# Segmented controls Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A segmented control groups two or more related buttons, usually at equal widths. It can represent a single choice; macOS also supports multiple simultaneous choices. A momentary control can instead perform related actions without retaining selection. ## Best practices Use segments for related object attributes, state, views, or actions when visible grouping or selection matters. Keep the interaction model consistent: all segments represent selection or all perform momentary actions. Aim for about 5–7 segments in a wide interface and no more than about 5 on iPhone. Equal widths and similarly sized titles or glyphs make the group easier to parse. ## Content Use text throughout a control or images throughout it rather than mixing those representations. Keep content footprints similar. Use title-case nouns or short noun phrases for textual choices; text-labeled controls generally need no introduction. ## Platform considerations Segmented controls are unsupported in watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Use segments to switch closely related subviews, such as two creation modes. Use a tab bar for separate top-level app sections. ### macOS Add introductory text when context is unclear, per-segment captions for unfamiliar glyphs, and individual tooltips when the app offers them. Prefer a tab view for switching panes in the main window body; segments can suit view switches in a toolbar or inspector. Consider spring loading: dragging over a segment and force-clicking with a Magic Trackpad can activate it while retaining the drag. ### tvOS A split view can make filtering easier to reach than a segmented control. Segments select as focus moves onto them, so keep other focusable elements far enough away to reduce accidental transitions. ### visionOS For icon segments, supply descriptive text for the tooltip the system presents when someone looks at the control. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 21, 2023.

# Apple HIG: presentation

Choose presentation from urgency, scope, duration, and whether the parent must remain usable. Reserve alerts for critical actionable interruptions; sheets for scoped tasks; popovers and panels for contextual tools; windows for sustained parallel work. Define saving, cancellation, resizing, focus, and return context before styling. Read platform sections for modal scope and spatial placement.

# Managing accounts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-accounts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Require an account only for essential core functionality; otherwise permit useful access without one. A consistent trusted sign-in method can reduce credential burden. ## Best practices Explain account benefits and signup requirements briefly and defer sign-in until commitment is needed, such as purchase after browsing. Consider Sign in with Apple; otherwise prefer passkeys on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. If retaining passwords, strengthen them with two-factor authentication. Name the actual available method, checking device capabilities instead of mentioning unsupported Face ID. Avoid a redundant app-specific biometric opt-in when the system already manages it. Reserve passcode terminology for device/Apple authentication rather than implying people should reuse it for an app account. ## Deleting accounts An app that supports account creation must also support deletion rather than only deactivation. Clearly disclose legally required retention or special processes; applicable legal requirements need separate verification. Provide a discoverable in-app deletion route or direct deletion-page link, not a buried policy link. Revoke Sign in with Apple tokens when deleting that account. Keep web and app flows comparably straightforward. If scheduling later deletion, retain immediate deletion too. State the expected completion time and notify when complete. Explain that deleting an account does not itself cancel an Apple auto-renewable subscription: billing continues until canceled, and subscription/refund management may still be needed. Provide management instructions. Support deletion even for subscriptions purchased elsewhere. ## TV provider accounts Use system TV Provider Authentication when available. Do not offer independent sign-out for a system-authenticated provider; if an option is necessary, direct to Settings > TV Provider. Privacy access controls are not a sign-out mechanism. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### tvOS Minimize remote data entry and prefer signup/authentication through another device with associated-domain credential suggestions. Shared account credentials can coexist with separate current-user profiles from tvOS 16; restore the current profile without repeatedly asking. For longer input, use a companion website; email keyboards can offer recent addresses. ### watchOS Use iCloud/keychain synchronization for credential autofill and retained app settings. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) [Sign in with Apple](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sign-in-with-apple) #### Developer documentation — Authentication Services #### Videos

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Alerts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. An alert interrupts to communicate urgent, critical information and useful actions, including problems, unexpected data loss, or important confirmations. ## Best practices Reserve alerts for situations that warrant immediate attention. Put informational status in context when no action is required. Common undoable deletions generally need no confirmation; uncommon irreversible destruction does. Avoid startup alerts: cached or placeholder content with a discreet problem explanation is often a better response to an unavailable network. ## Anatomy Alerts are modal and adapt their appearance to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS rather than using one universal layout. ## Content Use a title, optional message, and up to three buttons. iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS can include text fields; macOS and visionOS can include an icon and accessory view. macOS additionally supports a suppression checkbox and Help button. Use direct, neutral, approachable wording without blaming the person or concealing severity. The title should explain what happened, its context, and cause as concisely as possible, generally within two lines. Avoid a bare error label or code. Complete-sentence titles use sentence case and punctuation; fragments use title case without punctuation. Additional text should add information in brief complete sentences. Clear action labels should make button explanations unnecessary; if instructions are unavoidable, use device-neutral language such as choose and the exact title without quotation marks. Include an input field only when resolving the situation requires it, with secure entry for passwords. ## Buttons Use short, usually one- or two-word, title-case action labels without punctuation. Prefer specific outcomes over Yes/No or ambiguous OK; reserve OK for purely informational acknowledgment. A cancellation action is always Cancel. Place the expected/default action at the trailing end of a row or top of a stack, with cancellation generally leading or at the bottom. Apply destructive styling to destructive consequences the person did not deliberately request. A confirmation of an explicitly chosen destruction, such as Empty Trash, can retain a normal default action so Return confirms intent. Always provide Cancel alongside destructive actions, but do not make Cancel the default. To force a deliberate reading, consider no default. A single default acknowledgment button should be Done rather than Cancel. Support familiar alternate cancellation where appropriate: Home Screen exit on iOS/iPadOS; Escape or Command-Period on attached keyboards in iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS; Menu on the tvOS remote. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use action sheets for multiple choices following an intentional action. Keep titles and optional messages short to minimize scrolling, while accommodating enlarged accessibility text. ### macOS The app icon appears automatically but can be replaced. Repeating alerts can offer suppression; necessary details can use an accessory view, and Help can open documentation. Reserve a caution symbol for situations needing extra attention, particularly unexpected loss, rather than routine overwrite, save, or empty-trash tasks. ### visionOS In Shared Space, an alert sits slightly in front of its parent window and stays attached when the window moves. In Full Space, it centers in the wearer's field of view. An accessory view must be no taller than 154 pt and use a 16-pt corner radius. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: February 2, 2024, September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

item.text: The supplied description identifies five issues. Immediate account deletion is the highest priority, followed by missing accessible selection state and contradictory selection. The correction will move unrelated actions out of the control and reserve segments for closely related views, if the account page needs them.

item.aggregated_output:
# iPhone account control audit

## Scope and decisions

Reviewed `interface.md`, which supplies a textual description rather than executable UI or a screenshot. “Verified” below means explicitly stated in that file; it does not mean independently reproduced. Priority reflects potential harm and task blockage, not measured frequency.

Replace the nine-action segmented control with separately labeled account actions. Retain a segmented control only if product requirements identify a small set of closely related subviews. The actual action inventory and subview names are missing, so the illustrative names below are not a proposed final information architecture.

## Ranked verified findings

| Rank | Supplied observation and effect | Source-backed decision and correction |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Critical | Selecting Delete Account destroys data immediately. A view-selection gesture can cause irreversible loss. | Remove deletion from the segments. Give it a discoverable account action that opens an explicit consequence review and confirmation with Cancel before any deletion request. HIG distinguishes uncommon irreversible destruction from ordinary undoable deletion. [Alerts: Best practices and Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts#Best-practices); [Managing accounts: Deleting accounts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-accounts#Deleting-accounts). |
| 2 — High | Keyboard/assistive users hear no selected state. They cannot reliably determine the active view. | Expose each choice’s full name, role, and selected state; make selection and activation keyboard-accessible, and publish state changes through the platform’s semantic accessibility mechanism. Exact spoken wording is implementation-dependent. [Accessibility: Vision, Mobility, Speech](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision). |
| 3 — High | Two segments remain selected for a single-view choice. The control gives contradictory feedback about the displayed view. | Store one selected view identifier and derive both visible selection and accessibility state from it. Exactly one choice is selected and its corresponding view is displayed. Multiple simultaneous choices are described for macOS, not this iPhone single-view task. [Segmented controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls). |
| 4 — High | Long labels truncate to identical prefixes. People cannot distinguish destinations reliably before activating them. | Use short, distinct title-case nouns or noun phrases for related view choices, with full accessible names. If labels cannot fit legibly at supported text sizes and widths, replace the horizontal control with a layout that shows complete labels. [Segmented controls: Content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls#Content); [Accessibility: Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision). |
| 5 — Medium | Nine unrelated actions share the segmented control. Their relationship and interaction model are unclear, and the count compounds crowding. | Separate unrelated actions; segments on iOS switch closely related subviews. The source advises no more than about five segments on iPhone, not an absolute five-item validity rule. Do not merely split the nine unrelated actions into smaller segmented groups. [Segmented controls: Best practices and iOS, iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls#Best-practices). |

## Corrected behavior specification

The following is framework-agnostic. No Apple SDK types are required. Semantic roles must be mapped to the chosen runtime rather than copied as API names.

```text
Account page:
  relatedViews = product-approved closely related subviews, if any
  selectedView = one valid view ID
  accountActions = separately labeled actions outside view selection
  Delete Account = discoverable separate action

renderViewChoices():
  for each view:
    show short, distinct visible label
    expose full accessible name and appropriate selection-control role
    visibleSelected = (view.id == selectedView)
    accessibleSelected = visibleSelected
  show only the content belonging to selectedView
  if choices cannot fit with readable, distinguishable labels:
    use an alternative choice layout with full labels

activateView(id):
  require id in relatedViews
  atomically update selectedView, selected semantics, and visible content
  retain logical focus on activated choice
  never execute an account action

keyboardAndAssistiveInput:
  allow traversal and activation of every choice and action
  show keyboard focus separately from selection
  use the same activation handler for all input methods
  moving focus alone does not delete data or execute actions

activateDeleteAccount():
  open confirmation with title "Delete Account?"
  explain the actual data loss, reversibility, and completion time
  offer "Cancel" and "Delete Account"; use no default action
  move focus into confirmation and keep background controls inactive
  do not send a deletion request yet

cancelConfirmation():
  close confirmation; restore focus to Delete Account
  preserve account data and selectedView

confirmDeletion():
  require explicit activation of "Delete Account" in confirmation
  send one deletion request; prevent duplicate submissions
  expose pending status without claiming completion
  on failure: explain failure and offer recovery without claiming deletion
  on success: notify completion and leave the deleted account context
```

Choosing no default in the confirmation is a design decision supported as an option by the Alerts guidance; Cancel remains available and is not made the default. Support familiar cancellation, including Escape on an attached keyboard. In Assistive Access, the supplied accessibility guide requires two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions; add a second explicit confirmation in that mode before submitting deletion. [Alerts: Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts#Buttons); [Accessibility: Cognitive](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Cognitive).

Keep deletion straightforward and discoverable. Disclose actual retention and completion timing; if Apple auto-renewable subscriptions apply, explain that account deletion does not cancel them and provide management instructions. These are implementation requirements to resolve, not observed omissions.
